quiz.q: Why does John Rawls reject the utilitarian conception of justice?
options: Because it fails to maximize the total economic output and technological progress of modern industrial society.
Because it permits the sacrifice of individual rights and human dignity for the welfare of the majority.
Because it grants unconditional priority to personal liberty over the basic economic welfare of citizens.
Because it relies on an abstract social contract rather than historically observed political arrangements.
quiz.why: Rawls rejects utilitarianism because it treats individuals as means rather than ends, violating human dignity to maximize aggregate happiness.

quiz.q: What information do individuals behind the Veil of Ignorance possess in the original position?
options: Complete knowledge of their personal wealth, natural intelligence, and future socioeconomic position in the community.
Detailed awareness of their society's cultural traditions, religious doctrines, and dominant philosophical beliefs.
General knowledge of economics and psychology, but no awareness of their own specific personal advantages.
Definite foresight regarding which specific professions and talents will be most highly rewarded by society.
quiz.why: Individuals behind the veil of ignorance understand general laws of economics and psychology, but do not know their specific traits or social standing.

quiz.q: According to Rawls, why do rational individuals in the original position adopt the maximin decision rule?
options: To select the social arrangement where the worst possible outcome is safest and least disadvantageous.
To maximize the average utility and total economic wealth generated across the entire political community.
To ensure that all individuals receive identical shares of income, social status, and material wealth.
To prioritize economic redistribution over basic civil liberties and equal political rights for all.
quiz.why: The maximin principle directs rational persons facing uncertainty to select the option that makes the worst possible outcome as favorable as possible.

quiz.q: How does Rawls justify socioeconomic inequalities under the Difference Principle?
options: Inequalities are justified if they reward individuals strictly according to their natural superior talents and desert.
Inequalities are justified whenever they increase aggregate national income, regardless of who receives the benefits.
Inequalities are justified only when private ownership of productive resources is eliminated across all sectors.
Inequalities are justified only if they operate to the greatest benefit of the least advantaged.
quiz.why: Because natural distribution of talents is morally arbitrary, Rawls allows socioeconomic inequalities only if they maximize advantages for the least well-off.
